about: Cinematic sets from StarCraft II's campaign cutscenes, described in our own words: each look was written by an agent from pictures of the set (Blender renders of its pieces where the cutscene file puts them, and frames filmed in game), and its size in cells and camera count were measured from the file. Its name and files are the keys that find it in the game's data; nothing else here is extracted from the game. The pictures are in sc2-mapping-reference, under public/sets.

a-asteroids.name: A Asteroids
a-asteroids.look: A flat-topped slab of rock floating in open space, with a trail of smaller asteroids drifting away from it to the north and up. The slab is roughly 28 by 22 cells and about 20 deep, with a cracked, level stone top broken by a few clusters of jagged rock spires 2 to 4 cells tall and loose boulders near the edges; the whole set, counting the asteroid trail, spans about 75 by 128 cells and 76 high. There are no walls or roof: a camera standing on the top sees the rock floor, the spires, the edge of the slab and then empty sky with tumbling rocks. In the game the rock is grey-brown and the surroundings are black space filled with dim green smoky clouds and a few pale points of light, with a harsh white-blue light washing out the middle of the slab and one pale glowing patch on its north-west edge. The mood is quiet, eerie and otherworldly.
standsInFor: a meeting on a lone rock adrift in space
a vision, dream or afterlife scene outside any real place
a small landing on an asteroid or a shattered moon fragment
a quiet farewell or epilogue against an empty sky

alarak-bg.name: Alarak BG
alarak-bg.look: A small open platform with a single tall throne on it, floating alone in a starfield with no walls, roof or ground around it. The platform is a flat, symmetrical butterfly shape with scalloped, ribbed edges and a raised hexagonal pad at each of its four corners; the set measures about 4 by 6 cells, and the throne's back rises in a thin spike about 6 cells above the floor. The throne sits at the middle of the west edge facing east across the bare centre of the platform, and behind it stands a flat, see-through wall of small glowing blue hexagons. The platform is dark red-brown plated metal with paler stone-like panels and grey-blue trim, and the throne is angular and bladed. In the game it is very dark: the platform is almost a silhouette against blue-white stars, with a few small orange lights on the throne and a soft golden glow on the hexagon wall behind it.

armada.name: ARMADA
armada.look: Open space with a small fleet of fighter craft hanging in it, inside a star-field dome about 230 cells across; there is no floor, wall or room. The ships sit in three loose groups within an area of roughly 10 by 15 cells near the middle: about six larger swept-wing fighters with red blade-like wings and dark hulls, and about twenty-five small dark twin-pod drones with glowing engine ends, all facing the same way. The dome carries a huge purple planet with a bright violet rim that fills the upper sky in the north, south and west views, with a blue-violet nebula and dense stars elsewhere and a plain black band on part of it. In the game it is very dark: the ships read as black shapes with red glowing edges against deep blue and purple space.

b-wrangler-room.name: B - Wrangler Room
b-wrangler-room.look: A large round machine chamber inside a plain grey panelled sphere about 18 cells across, with a reclined chair or cradle with a red headrest lying on a circular pad at the centre. The chamber itself is about 13 cells across and 3 high: a floor of metal walkways and dark floor panels with railings runs out from the centre like spokes to a ring walkway against the wall. Six heavy machine pillars with small lit screens stand in a ring around the centre, each inside its own railed bay, and thick pipes bend from them to a wide drum that hangs from the ceiling over the chair. The walls and ceiling are dark grey armour plating with hexagonal recessed panels, worn bare metal and faded orange hazard paint; above the centre the ceiling opens into a short hex-panelled well, and below the walkways six blocky housings hang into the empty lower half of the sphere. No in-game capture exists, so its lighting and mood are unknown.

building-01.name: Building_01
building-01.look: The outside of a grand classical stone building, seen as a shell with no interior: a three-storey block about 17 by 35 cells and 20 high, standing on a paved stone terrace. Its long west front has a ground-floor colonnade of fluted columns with carved capitals at the top of a wide flight of steps with balustrades, tall grids of dark windows above, a heavy cornice, and two gabled pavilions with green copper domed roofs on top. Four large white and dark-grey angular machine pylons with thin glowing strips stand on the steps against the facade, a futuristic addition to the old stonework, and a smaller one sits on the roof terrace between the pavilions. The south end wall is blank panelled stone above a rusticated base, and an open paved plaza with a low balustrade wall runs south of the building. Everything is pale cream sandstone except the green roofs and the white pylons; the one usable in-game capture shows it at night or in deep shadow, with hard low light raking across the plaza and the pylons.

a crowd gathered on the steps of a grand hall
an establishing shot of an old city district fitted with new technology

c-wrangler-room.name: C - Wrangler Room
c-wrangler-room.look: A round terran machine room with a restraint couch on a dais at its centre and six operator stations ringed around it, all inside a much larger plain grey panelled shell. The deck is about 12 cells across and the ceiling about 3 cells up, inside a shell roughly 21 by 17 cells and 17 high; the deck is a web of metal walkways radiating from the central dais over dark sunken panels. Each of the six stations is a heavy reclined seat in a railed bay with a small screen and a tall machine column behind it, all facing inward, and above the dais hangs a fat machine drum circled by a thick pipe ring with a ring of lights. A curved wall of dark hexagon-framed panels with worn orange markings closes the north and east sides behind a handrail, while the south and west are open to the blank grey shell; everything is scuffed grey steel, and the only colour is the couch's bright yellow straps, blue cables and a red panel. No in-game capture is usable, so the game's lighting and mood are unknown.

cargo.name: Cargo
cargo.look: A long, narrow pile of terran cargo with no room around it: no floor, walls or ceiling are part of the set. It runs about 9 cells wide by 28 long and up to 4 high, with stacked white-and-black hard-shell crates, cases and canisters with yellow hazard marks along the northern two thirds, and a cluster of six or so rusty grey-and-blue walker mechs with red and green details parked at the south end. One crate lies open showing rows of red-tipped shells with a rifle resting beside it, and a few small purple translucent objects sit on top of crates. In the game it is lit with hard, cold blue-white light against black, so the crates glow at the edges and everything beyond them falls into darkness.

chips-stuff.name: CHIPS STUFF
chips-stuff.look: Not a place: three standing figures and one machine on an empty ground, with no floor, walls or backdrop, spread over about 7 by 4 cells. At the west end stand a fair-haired person in a pale blue dress uniform with gold shoulder pieces and trim, arms held out in a rest pose, and two figures in dark grey armour with long coats, one in a visored helmet, facing each other; a pair of small black goggles lies on the ground in front of them. About four cells to the east is a dark metal jointed arm, roughly three cells tall, with round pivot drums, a bundle of black cables, a box mount at its top and a camera-like head with a small blue lens at its lower end. Everything is dark grey or black metal and cloth except the blue and gold uniform. The in-game captures are all black, so its mood in the game is unknown.

city.name: city
city.look: A cluster of ruined, overgrown stone temples standing in the open with no ground or sky of its own, about 89 by 85 cells and 43 high. One very large stepped pyramid temple with curved buttresses, horn-like spires and a glowing cyan crystal on top fills the east side (roughly 40 by 60 cells, with a second, smaller temple joined to its north end by a stair); a medium pyramid temple sits in the north-west and a small one in the middle, each with its own cyan crystal. Between them stand tall bronze-coloured curled towers and spires, some broken and one with a dark arched face, and two bright yellow-gold pillars wrapped in green vines, while a curved row of about twenty low mossy stone wall blocks arcs across the south-west. Everything is grey-green weathered stone streaked with moss, with tarnished bronze and gold metalwork. The in-game captures are almost black, showing only dim blue-grey silhouettes and blue crystals, so the real mood is not known.

communicator-ambient-bridge-probes.name: Communicator (Ambient_Bridge_Probes)
communicator-ambient-bridge-probes.look: A terran warship bridge: one long eight-sided room about 15 by 11 cells and roughly 4 cells high under a heavy ribbed ceiling. At the west end a raised command deck with railings, two short stairways and a small console sits in front of a wrap-around band of large windows; the main floor behind it is dark plate and grey tread-plate with a round machine in the centre whose twin hangs from the ceiling above it. The side and east walls are waist-high armoured panels topped by window-like bays full of dark pipework and round turbine housings, framed by blue-grey pillars with gold filigree trim, wolf-head crests and cyan light strips. There is a doorway in each long wall near the command deck, and a figure in heavy powered armour stands beside the north one. The in-game captures are black, so the mood under game lighting is unknown; under even light it is cold blue-grey steel with cyan glow and gold accents.

corridoor.name: Corridoor
corridoor.look: A long, narrow terran service corridor with an octagonal cross-section, about 2 cells wide, 17 cells long and 2.5 high, running north to south between two larger rooms. Repeating octagonal steel ribs frame every cell; behind them the side walls are open bays of thick red and grey pipes, vents and grilles, the ceiling carries pipe bundles and small white light panels, and the floor is grey tread-plate tiles. Each end opens into a tapering six-sided room about 14 by 9 cells and 5 high, walled in dark grey angular armour panels with small orange markers and a doorway, but drawn with no floor or furniture in the neutral renders. In the game the corridor is very dark, nearly black metal lit only by the cold white ceiling panels, with a green glow from the room at the far end; the mood is tense and claustrophobic.

courtyard-smx3-cutscene-mp03-020.name: Courtyard (SMX3_Cutscene_MP03_020)
courtyard-smx3-cutscene-mp03-020.look: A speaker's balcony set high in the face of a tall dark-grey terran tower, with a lectern at its railing and a wood-panelled room opening behind it. The tower front is about 34 cells wide and 64 tall, a tapering slab of grey panels with pale stone bands; the balcony juts out about 18 cells up on two white brackets and is roughly 10 cells wide by 8 deep. The balcony floor is grey-green marble tile with pale inlaid bands, ringed by a low white parapet with beige stone posts, and the lectern (black top, microphone, gold chevron-and-star emblem) stands at the middle of the outer edge. Behind it, a few dark steps lead through a wide white-framed opening into a room with a dark wood floor, an orange-red rug, panelled walls, bookshelves and a framed painting; three tall blue-framed screens hang in front of the tower beside and below the balcony. There is no ground or courtyard floor in the set, and in the game the balcony is lit very bright white against black surroundings, with the room behind dark.

cutscene-aiur01debrief-set-cutscene-aiur.name: Cutscene_Aiur01Debrief set (Cutscene_Aiur01Debrief)
cutscene-aiur01debrief-set-cutscene-aiur.look: A far-background miniature of a ruined city on a crag: a tight cluster of sand-gold spires, stepped towers and a domed temple perched on a jumble of brown rock, with a much larger rock mass rearing up behind and over it. The buildings fill only about 25 by 20 cells and stand some 45 high, inside a rock pile about 77 by 85 cells across and 91 tall. The tallest features are a thin curved blade-shaped wall of gold and dark grey panels standing against the rock face on the east side, a smaller blade beside it, a pale obelisk-like tower and a striped cone-shaped tower at the front, with a tuft of green overgrowth on the western buildings. There is no ground, floor or sky: the rocks float in empty space with gaps between them, so it only works seen from the south or south-east, from a distance. Colours are warm ochre, cream and dark slate on the buildings and rust-brown on the rock; no in-game capture shows its lighting.

A short flight of pale stone stairs with gold trim and a few clumps of grass and yellow-leaved plants sit behind the rim to the north-west. The five other masses to the south are bare boulders and crags of the same cracked brown and rust-orange rock, 5 to 15 cells across, that read as distant background. No in-game capture exists, so its lighting and mood are unknown.

a lookout or hiding place among crags in grassland
a camp or meeting spot in wild country near old ruins

guided-models.name: Guided Models
guided-models.look: A miniature city seen from the air at dusk, built for a shot that looks out of the toothed mouth of a living, fleshy ship as pods drop toward the ground. The city is a flat square of pinkish-brown ground about 90 cells a side, printed with a street map and ring roads, carrying a hundred or so low-detail white-and-black tower blocks and a few detailed grey-blue terran buildings, inside a half-dome painted backdrop about 305 by 215 cells and 114 high. The backdrop shows a stormy blue-grey sky with an orange sunset on the horizon, a distant skyline with a large stepped pyramid tower, and the dark shape of a huge ship hanging in the clouds. The foreground piece is a small organic frame only about 7 cells wide and 4.5 high: red-brown flesh and bone ribs, rows of teeth around a wide opening, yellow sacs and a dark segmented tentacle. A third piece is a scatter of small red glowing organic pods strung out for about 100 cells along the line of sight, as if falling toward the city.
standsInFor: looking down on a city from an organic ship's hatch before a landing
drop pods falling on a city at dusk
a distant city skyline under a storm sky with a capital ship overhead

interior-cutscene-rohanaintro.name: Interior (Cutscene_RohanaIntro)
interior-cutscene-rohanaintro.look: A long, vaulted protoss hall lined with upright blue-glowing pods, ending in a round open balcony that looks out on the stacked hull tiers of a huge ship. The hall is a straight nave roughly 10 cells wide and 30 or more long, running north-south, with four bays down each side; each bay holds a tall dark pod with an oval pane of blue crystal-like glass, set on a raised plinth with small pointed posts in front. At the south end a short flight of steps climbs between two pointed blue arched panels to a large dark doorway; at the north end the floor widens into a circular platform with a patterned grille in the floor, a small ringed floor pedestal carrying a hovering device, and a low curved rail in front of the open view. Everything is pale ivory and grey-brown plating with cream inlaid line patterns on the floor, ribbed arches overhead and a few gold fins along the ceiling spine. The set's listed size (580 x 852 cells) comes from the far-off backdrop hull pieces, not the hall; no in-game capture exists, so the lighting mood is unknown.

a walk down a hall of sleeping warriors or stored pods
a character at a balcony rail looking out over a vast ship or fleet structure
an arrival through a grand doorway into a ceremonial chamber

kerrigan-zsm-zeratul.look: A small patch of dense alien jungle: a mossy rock ledge under a cluster of thick, twisted tree trunks whose flat, spiky leaf crowns close overhead like umbrellas. The whole clump is about 14 by 11 cells and 12 high, but it has no ground or sky beyond its own edge, and the cameras all work in one corner of it, on a ledge roughly 2 to 3 cells across at the south-west. The ledge is grey-pink layered rock covered in bright green moss, with big yellow-green ferns, hanging vines, and bushes of small orange and dark green star-shaped leaves in the foreground; the tree crowns are green with red veins. In the game it is lit low and moody, with dark olive greens against a pure black background, so the place reads as a clearing deep in a forest at night.

korhalspace.name: KorhalSpace
korhalspace.look: This set has no room: it is two flat, upright glow sheets and one standing human figure in empty space. The larger sheet is about 12 cells wide and 6 tall and stands a few cells north of the figure; a smaller one, roughly 4 by 4 cells, stands to the west at a right angle to it. Under neutral light both sheets are plain white with no texture, so they read as light sources or a bright doorway glow behind the figure rather than as walls. The figure is a woman with tied-up brown hair in a white and grey-blue bodysuit with dark red gloves and boots, arms crossed, standing at the centre and much smaller than the sheets. main-set.name: Main_Set
main-set.look: A wide, low-ceilinged terran ship bay where a curved corridor passes through a central hall, about 42 by 22 cells and 4 high. The hall is a rounded-corner room roughly 20 cells across with a curved, windowed back wall on the north side; two corridor arms curve away east and west, and a short stub on the south side ends in a closed blast door reached by three short ramps with handrails. Square pillars with pipes and wall-mounted machinery stand around the middle, railed pits in the floor hold rows of crates or bunks, and black equipment racks and cluttered workbenches sit along the sides. Everything is riveted grey-blue steel with rust on the panels, a hexagon-panelled ceiling, heavy overhead pipes and a pale hex-tiled deck with checker markings. In the game it is dark and cold, lit in hard white pools on the floor and ramps with the walls falling into black.

monitors.name: Monitors
monitors.look: This is not a room but a handful of loose flat screens and one small white panel floating in empty space, spread over about 31 by 14 cells with no floor, walls or ceiling. At the west end a curved bank of about a dozen small rectangular monitor panels (blank white or pale grey under neutral light) stands about 4 cells wide beside a large black square sheet some 4 to 5 cells across. normal-hallways-door.name: Normal Hallways + Door
normal-hallways-door.look: Two long curved corridors of a golden protoss ship, each an arc about 70 cells long and 8 wide, lying side by side and nearly touching near the set's cameras, where a tall ornate pointed door leaf stands on the floor. Between the ribs the roof is open, so in the game the starry sky and a faint blue hexagon shield show above. Beside the corridors, well outside them, sits part of a much larger round golden hall (a half-ring floor about 130 cells across with a central drum and tall ribbed walls) as a backdrop. In the game the light is warm gold with hard dark shadows and blue glints, and one arch glows bright yellow-white.

nova-bridge.name: Nova Bridge
nova-bridge.look: The bridge of a small terran ship: a long, narrow room about 7 cells wide and 16 long, with a raised deck some 2.5 cells under a low ribbed ceiling. A straight central walkway of striped grey deck plates runs from an open rear end north to the nose, where two white-and-black pilot stations with teal screens sit side by side in a sunken pit behind a wide black console, facing a large forward window. Left and right of the pit, railed side platforms each hold a brown padded chair with a small monitor, and a further console with teal screens stands on the west side behind them; big slanted side windows and heavy white angular pillars line both walls. Everything is clean white and mid-grey panelling over dark grey machined hull, with teal and blue screen glow. The one usable in-game capture is a close-up of a console, which shows a dark, cold blue-green mood lit mostly by the screens.

pipes.name: Pipes
pipes.look: A scatter of loose industrial pipes, hoses and cable bundles hanging in empty space, with no floor, walls or ceiling of their own. About twenty pieces are spread over roughly 23 by 16 cells and 13 cells of height: thick ribbed hoses with pale metal clamps, some running level in gentle S-bends and some standing upright with an elbow at the top, plus thin paired conduits and wispy cable strands with small clips. The west side holds a cluster of short curved hose pieces, while the east side has longer straight runs and L-shaped drops. Everything is dark grey to black rubber and steel with light grey bands, and one thick hose carries a strip of coloured wires. In the game they show against pure black, lit cold blue-white, with one pair of conduit ends glowing brightly.

set-guide-do-not-import.name: Set (Guide) DO NOT IMPORT
